머리카락.x: My younger sibling has long hair.
머리카락.t: In everyday speech 머리 alone often means hair: 머리를 잘랐어요 = I got a haircut.

수업.x: What time does today's class end?
수업.t: 'Take a class' is 수업을 듣다 (literally 'listen to a class').

인터넷.t: 'Online / via the internet' = 인터넷으로. Pronounced [인터넫]; before 이/을: [인터네시], [인터네슬].

무겁다.t: ㅂ irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel — 무겁다 → 무거워요.

곧.forms: 곧 + verb: 곧 도착해요, 곧 시작할 거예요
A은/는 곧 B이다 — 'A is (nothing other than) B'
곧.m: that is, namely, in other words; soon
곧.ex: 사람들은 흔히 시간은 곧 돈이라고 말해요.
곧.x: People often say that time is money.
곧.e: Homonym warning: the same 곧 also means 'soon'; context tells you which.
곧.t: In 'A은/는 곧 B이다', 곧 means 'is none other than' — common in proverbs and formal writing.

모습.m: appearance, figure, look; the way someone looks
모습.x: The child looks so lovely when smiling.
모습.t: It usually follows a modifier: 웃는 모습 'how someone looks smiling', 예전 모습 'how it used to look'.

회색.ex: 오늘은 회색 바지에 흰 셔츠를 입었어요.
회색.x: Today I wore gray pants with a white shirt.
회색.t: 회색 하늘 means a gloomy, overcast sky.

고객.ex: 고객의 의견을 잘 듣는 것이 중요해요.
고객.x: It's important to listen carefully to customers' opinions.
고객.t: Staff address customers as 고객님 — very polite, common in phone calls and announcements.

예방하다.ex: 물을 자주 마시면 감기를 예방하는 데 도움이 돼요.
예방하다.x: Drinking water often helps prevent colds.

공공장소.x: Please don't talk loudly on the phone in public places.

환승하다.x: Get off at the next station and transfer to Line 2.
환승하다.t: In casual speech people say 갈아타다; 환승 appears on signs and announcements.

유통 기한.x: The milk's expiration date was yesterday.
유통 기한.e: Literally 'circulation period limit': how long it may be sold.
유통 기한.t: Often written 유통기한; since 2023 Korean labels mostly show 소비 기한 'use-by date' instead.

완성.ex: 이 그림은 완성까지 일 년이 걸렸어요.
완성.x: This painting took a year to complete.

사직서.x: He handed in his resignation letter this morning.

기획.x: I'm in charge of planning this event.
기획.e: Literally 'aim and map out' a project.
기획.t: 기획 is planning a project or product at work; 계획 is any plan, including personal ones.

전등.x: The room was dark, so I turned on the light.
전등.t: In speech, 불을 켜다 'turn on the light' is more common than 전등을 켜다.

시청률.ex: 그 예능 프로그램은 시청률이 아주 높아요.
시청률.x: That variety show has very high ratings.
시청률.t: Pronounced [시청뉼]: after ㅇ, the ㄹ of 률 turns into ㄴ.

짐작하다.m: to guess, to estimate, to imagine
짐작하다.ex: 그동안 얼마나 힘들었는지 짐작할 수 있어요.
짐작하다.x: I can imagine how hard it has been for you all this time.
짐작하다.e: Originally meant carefully pouring wine, gauging just the right amount.
짐작하다.t: 짐작 is an intuitive guess; 추측 sounds more reasoned and formal.

선입견.x: I try to meet people without preconceptions.

첫눈.x: We promised to meet on the day of the first snow.
첫눈.t: Pronounced [천눈]. Romantic in Korean culture: couples promise to meet when the first snow falls, and folk belief says your love comes true if your balsam nail dye (봉숭아 물) lasts until then.

수족관.x: I saw lots of amazing fish at the aquarium.
수족관.e: Literally 'water-family hall': 수족 means creatures that live in water.
수족관.t: Pronounced [수족꽌]: ㄱ makes the next ㄱ tense. Big ones often call themselves 아쿠아리움.

세상에.forms: 세상에! · stronger: 세상에나! · 세상에, 이럴 수가!
세상에.m: oh my God!, good heavens!, my goodness
세상에.ex: 세상에, 이 많은 음식을 혼자 다 만들었어요?
세상에.x: Good heavens, you made all this food by yourself?
세상에.e: 세상 'the world' (literally 'upon the world') + 에 'in' — as if saying 'in all the world, how can this be?'
세상에.t: Shows amazement or shock, good or bad. 세상에나 is stronger and sounds a bit older or more motherly.

고령화 사회.ex: 한국은 빠르게 고령화 사회가 되고 있습니다.
고령화 사회.x: Korea is quickly becoming an aging society.
고령화 사회.e: Literally 'society becoming high-aged'; -화 works like English '-ization'.

구축하다.m: to build, to establish, to set up (a system or network)
구축하다.ex: 정부는 새로운 교통 시스템을 구축할 계획입니다.
구축하다.x: The government plans to build a new transportation system.
구축하다.t: Pronounced [구추카다]; used for abstract structures like systems, networks and relationships, not buildings.

일석이조.m: killing two birds with one stone
일석이조.ex: 운동하면서 돈도 벌 수 있으니까 일석이조예요.
일석이조.x: I can exercise and earn money too, so it's two birds with one stone.
일석이조.e: Literally 'one stone, two birds'—exactly like the English idiom.
일석이조.t: The native proverb 꿩 먹고 알 먹기 means the same thing and sounds more casual.
rel: eat the pheasant and its eggs

신경을 쓰다.forms: 신경을 써요 · 신경을 썼어요 · 신경 쓰지 마세요 (ㅡ drops)
신경을 쓰다.m: to pay attention to, to care about; to worry about
신경을 쓰다.ex: 외모에 너무 신경을 쓰지 않아도 돼요.
신경을 쓰다.x: You don't have to worry so much about your looks.
신경을 쓰다.e: 신경 = nerves; literally 'to use one's nerves' on something.
신경을 쓰다.t: 신경 쓰지 마세요 means 'Don't worry about it'; casual 신경 꺼 is a rude 'Mind your own business.'

구독 서비스.ex: 안 쓰는 구독 서비스는 해지하는 게 좋아요.
구독 서비스.x: It's best to cancel subscription services you don't use.
구독 서비스.e: 구독 'subscription' (literally 'buy to read') + 서비스 from English 'service'.
구독 서비스.t: Covers streaming, music, meal kits and regular deliveries. Cancel a subscription: 해지하다.

천명하다.m: to declare, to proclaim, to make clear
천명하다.x: The government declared a war on corruption.
천명하다.t: Very formal and mostly written; in conversation use 밝히다 or 선언하다.

화합물.x: Water is a compound made of hydrogen and oxygen.
화합물.t: Pronounced [화함물]: ㅂ before ㅁ becomes ㅁ (nasalization).

고독사.ex: 1인 가구가 늘면서 고독사 문제도 심각해지고 있습니다.
고독사.x: As single-person households increase, the problem of lonely deaths is becoming serious.

포용.ex: 다양한 문화를 포용하는 사회가 되어야 해요.
포용.x: We need to become a society that embraces diverse cultures.
포용.t: Don't confuse 포용 (embracing people or ideas) with 포옹 (a physical hug).

부각하다.m: to highlight, to bring into relief, to emphasize
부각하다.ex: 언론은 이번 사건의 심각성을 크게 부각했습니다.
부각하다.x: The media strongly highlighted how serious the incident was.
부각하다.e: Literally 'carving in relief' so it floats up from the surface.

주력하다.m: to concentrate on, to focus (one's efforts) on
주력하다.ex: 우리 회사는 신제품 개발에 주력하고 있습니다.
주력하다.x: Our company is focusing on developing new products.

울컥.forms: 울컥하다 · 눈물이 울컥 나다 · 화가 울컥 치밀다
울컥.m: with a sudden surge (of emotion), welling up; suddenly (throwing up)
울컥.ex: 엄마의 편지를 읽다가 울컥 눈물이 났어요.
울컥.x: While reading my mom's letter, tears suddenly welled up.
울컥.e: A mimetic word for something surging up all at once — also food.
울컥.t: 울컥하다 can mean choking up with tears or flaring up in anger; context decides.
rel: to choke up; to flare up

수박 겉 핥기.forms: 수박 겉 핥기로 + verb · 수박 겉 핥기식
수박 겉 핥기.m: superficial treatment; only scratching the surface
수박 겉 핥기.ex: 시간이 없어서 수박 겉 핥기로 책을 읽었어요.
수박 겉 핥기.x: I didn't have time, so I only skimmed the surface of the book.
수박 겉 핥기.e: Licking a watermelon's rind, you never taste the sweet fruit inside.
수박 겉 핥기.t: Pronounced [수박 걷 할끼]; often 수박 겉 핥기식 공부 'superficial studying.'

애증.ex: 저는 이 도시에 대해 애증의 감정을 느껴요.
애증.x: I have love-hate feelings about this city.

요지부동.x: No matter how much we try to persuade him, my father won't budge.
요지부동.e: Literally 'shake it and it doesn't move'.
요지부동.t: Used for stubborn people and also for numbers that won't change: 집값이 요지부동이다.

오죽하면.m: how bad must it be that … (you can imagine how bad)
오죽하면.ex: 오죽하면 그 착한 사람이 화를 냈겠어요?
오죽하면.x: Imagine how bad it must have been for such a kind person to get angry.
오죽하면.e: 오죽 'how (very)' + 하다 + -면 'if': 'how bad must it be, if …'.
오죽하면.t: Pronounced [오주카면]. Asks for sympathy: things were so bad that someone did something unusual. Usually ends in -았/었겠어요?

덤핑.ex: 정부는 외국산 철강에 반덤핑 관세를 부과했습니다.
덤핑.x: The government imposed anti-dumping duties on foreign steel.
덤핑.e: From English 'dumping'; also used casually for selling goods off cheap.
덤핑.t: In daily life 덤핑 often just means a clearance sale at rock-bottom prices, e.g. 덤핑 판매.

국내총생산.x: This year's GDP grew 2% over last year.
국내총생산.e: A word-for-word translation of 'gross domestic product'.
국내총생산.t: Pronounced [궁내총생산] by nasalization; in speech Koreans usually just say GDP (지디피).

검경.x: The prosecution and police worked together to investigate the crime ring.
검경.e: A short combo of 검찰 'prosecution' and 경찰 'police'.
검경.t: Mostly appears in news compounds like 검경 갈등 or 검경 수사권 조정.

쾌락주의.ex: 쾌락주의는 즐거움을 삶의 최고 가치로 봅니다.
쾌락주의.x: Hedonism sees pleasure as the highest value in life.
쾌락주의.t: 쾌락 often has a sensual or indulgent ring, so use 즐거움 for everyday 'fun' or 'enjoyment'.

무력감.ex: 아무것도 할 수 없다는 무력감에 빠졌어요.
무력감.x: I sank into a sense of helplessness, feeling I couldn't do anything.
무력감.t: Pronounced [무력깜]; often with 빠지다 or 느끼다.

궤양.x: I got an ulcer in my mouth because of stress.

소박미.ex: 이 그릇은 장식이 없어서 오히려 소박미가 있어요.
소박미.x: This bowl has no decoration, which actually gives it a simple charm.
소박미.t: Pronounced [소방미]: ㄱ before ㅁ becomes ㅇ (nasalization).

토사구팽.m: being discarded once one's usefulness is over
토사구팽.x: Once the election was over, he was tossed aside.
토사구팽.e: Literally 'when the rabbit dies, the hunting dog gets cooked'.
토사구팽.t: Usually 토사구팽을 당하다 'to be used and then thrown away'.

위정자.ex: 위정자들은 국민의 목소리에 귀를 기울여야 합니다.
위정자.x: Those in power must listen to the voice of the people.
위정자.e: -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자, 위정자.
위정자.t: Formal and literary; often used with a critical edge toward people in power.

선공후사.m: putting public interest before private interest
선공후사.x: Public officials should put the public interest before their own.
